svg.text: Paths from here (a sampler; none is the 'right' one)
Keep doing what you do
no need to change; but keep skills fresh, since even leadership styles date
Work toward promotion
know the process; is it the level or cash, respect, scope you want? be as impactful
as they were at promotion
Work less
80 percent time for 20 percent less pay (Jens Rantil); be clear where hours come
from and align with your manager
Change teams
keep context and capital, restart fresh; like a new low-level character who knows
the game (Burin Asavesna)
Build a new specialty
on boundaries interesting things happen; maybe move tracks (Lou Bichard to product
management)
Explore
rotations or short gigs; one engineer tried three teams in two years and chose
research
Take a management role
the pendulum (Charity Majors): manager is not a promotion; commit about two years;
hybrid roles only with experience of both (Will Larson)
First direct reports
for a goal that needs it, for leverage, or at the top of the ladder; spend time as
a line manager first (Amanda Walker)
Find or invent your niche
'holes shaped like you' (Molly Graham); beware roles that sound tailor-made but
exhaust you; make 70 percent of the job energising (Fabianna Tassini)
Same job, new employer
avoid the 'rebound' job; ask what staff means there; check the interview slate
Up a level, or down a level
easier in a domain you know; compare titles on levels.fyi; down a level can fix
foundations (Josh Kaderlan)
Own your path
a startup (build a cash safety net first); independent consulting (needs a network,
less glamorous); change careers (Peter Lyons runs a retreat for programmers)
